newsitem.title: INDIA: India hunts for shipwreck survivors as hope fades.
newsitem.headline: India hunts for shipwreck survivors as hope fades.

text.p: Indian navy and coast guard helicopters scanned the choppy waters of the Arabian Sea off Bombay on Friday in a hunt for 20 people missing after a shipwreck, but officials said hopes for recovery were fading.
"It's been more than 24 hours," said a defence spokesman. "Under this sort of conditions it's very, very difficult for them to survive."
Four people died and nine were rescued after the M.V. Arcadia Pride, a 13,672-tonne vessel loaded with 12,000 tonnes of sulphur, sank suddenly in squally weather on Thursday, officials said.
But the rest of the 33 people aboard are still missing.
Two Navy vessels were patrolling the waters where the ship went down, seven nautical miles off Bombay's coast, the defence official told Reuters.
Five helicopters were flying regular sorties in the hope of picking up survivors, but none had been found, he added.
"The 'copters are undertaking search operations, but the sea is very rough, and they haven't found anything so far," the official said.
The search would continue until every possibility had been exhausted, he added.
"They will review the situation again and again," he said, when asked if the search would be called off.
"They will not take any chance. Let me put it this way, they will not leave any stone unturned to find anyone."
A senior port official said the wreck of the ship would not block the movement of other vessels into Bombay port.
"No, it won't affect the movement of other ships," he said.

In another incident on Thursday near the eastern city of Calcutta, police said all 20 crew were rescued after the Panama-flag M.V. Green Opal sank in the Hooghly river following a collision with a barge.
Port officials said there was little hope of recovering the 7,000 tonnes of steel coils and billets the vessel was carrying.
